procedure.name: Engine Oil Change
procedure.description: A guided proof-of-concept workflow for performing an engine oil change.

requiredEquipment: Jack and jack stands or approved lifting equipment
requiredMaterials: Correct engine oil for the specific vehicle configuration
Replacement drain plug washer if required
safetyWarnings: Park the vehicle on a stable, level surface.
Allow hot engine components and oil to cool before beginning.
Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.
Verify all vehicle-specific specifications using an authoritative service source before performing maintenance.
preparation: Confirm the exact vehicle and engine configuration.
Verify the correct oil type, capacity, filter, and service specifications.
Gather all required tools, materials, and PPE.
Park on a level surface and secure the vehicle.
Allow the engine to cool to a safe working temperature.

steps.title: Prepare the vehicle
steps.instruction: Secure the vehicle and establish safe access to the oil drain and filter locations.

steps.title: Position the drain pan
steps.instruction: Place the drain pan beneath the engine oil drain location.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil
steps.instruction: Remove the drain plug using the appropriate tool and allow the used oil to drain completely.

steps.title: Replace the oil filter
steps.instruction: Remove the old filter and install the correct replacement according to verified service information.

steps.title: Reinstall the drain plug
steps.instruction: Reinstall the drain plug and any required replacement washer using verified vehicle-specific specifications.

steps.title: Add new engine oil
steps.instruction: Add the verified type and quantity of engine oil through the engine oil fill location.

steps.title: Verify the service
steps.instruction: Check the oil level and inspect the drain plug and filter areas for leaks.

completionChecklist: Drain plug area checked for leaks
Oil filter area checked for leaks
Used oil and filter prepared for proper recycling or disposal

dataStatus.notice: Vehicle-specific capacities, torque specifications, fluid specifications, part numbers, and service intervals must be verified before real-world use.
